Class SlotElement

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.slot.SlotElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public final class SlotElement extends AbstractPanelElement
A registered MKC slot presented as a PanelElement, the keystone of the everything-is-a-panel model. A slot is just another element you drop into a panel, alongside buttons and labels.

What this element does, and what it deliberately does not

A slot has two separable layers:
  • Registration, a real, server-synced CreatedSlot in menu.slots. Built at menu-construction time via CreatedSlots; untouched by this class.
  • Placement, where it sits on screen. This is what SlotElement owns. Each frame, in layer 2 of ContainerScreenLayers, it resolves its panel-relative position to screen space and writes it into the live slot's own Slot.x/y. (Layer 2: after vanilla has drawn the vanilla slots, before it draws the created ones.) It also draws the recessed 18×18 frame, which is panel chrome.
It does not draw the item, the count, the durability bar, the hover highlight, or a ghost icon. Vanilla does, its extractSlots walks menu.slots and draws this slot at the x/y written here, through the same extractSlot call it uses for a vanilla slot; its getHoveredSlot finds it the same way. That is the presentation half of CreatedSlot's substitutability contract: a third party's slot hook, or any mod reading slot.x/y, sees a created slot and a vanilla slot as the same thing because there is no MenuKit slot pass for them to differ in. (This is the model CustomContainerScreen has always used on MenuKit's own screens.)

Located, not held, the menu-attach lifecycle

A SlotElement does not hold a slot reference; it holds the slot's stable Address and resolves the live in-menu slot from the current screen's menu each frame (through CreatedSlotAdapter's session-cached binding). This is what lets one statically-registered panel work on every screen: the survival inventory and the creative screen carry different slot instances for the same logical slot (creative wraps it in a SlotWrapper and projects it onto a throwaway menu), and a held reference would bind to one and be wrong on the other. The position is written to whichever instance is in menu.slots, the wrapper on creative. because that is the one vanilla draws.

Parked when not presented

At the end of each frame (SlotElementRegistry.parkUnpresented(AbstractContainerMenu)) every attached element whose panel did not render it this frame moves its slot off-screen. So a slot whose panel is hidden, out of region, or hidden by the window is at a position vanilla neither draws nor hit-tests next frame, rather than wherever it was last drawn; one that was presented keeps its position, so hover between frames agrees with the picture. (CreatedSlot.isActive() covers the panel-hidden case on its own; parking covers the rest.)

An element in an overlay-positioned panel (layer 4) writes its position after vanilla's slot pass, so vanilla draws it one frame late and under the overlay's chrome. Created slots belong in flow panels; nothing places them in overlays today.

Why a slot stays live under its own panel's claim

A slot's item interaction is owned by vanilla: a click flows through AbstractContainerScreen.mouseClicked → slotClicked(getHoveredSlot()), and MenuKit's library-owned getHoveredSlot interception (CreatedSlotInput) makes the registered slot win over a vanilla slot it covers. An opaque panel claims its whole rectangle (§0065: no holes), so the claim routes a point over this element's slot back to vanilla (presentsSlotAt(InputContext)): the panel's own slot hovers and clicks, while anything else under the panel stays inert. On a transparent panel the slot is simply not solid (isElementOpaque() is false), so it claims nothing itself. SlotElementRegistry tells the library's screen hook which panels currently host a SlotElement.

      public static SlotElement.Builder builder()
      A slot element: SlotElement.builder().slot(CreatedSlots.groupId(panel, group), i).at(x, y).build(). The shared vocabulary applies: at, visibleWhen (on top of the slot's own reveal), tooltip (shown over an empty slot; a slot with an item shows the item's). A slot is never solid, so opaque has no effect.
